paper.title_en: Environment-induced phase modulation of threshold resonances in low-energy <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>2</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>2</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> nuclear reactions
paper.abstract_en: Low-energy <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow></math> reactions in condensed-matter environments (where <math><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></math> denotes <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>2</mn></mmultiscripts></math>) exhibit several reported features, including suppression of the neutron channel, enhanced angular anisotropy, plateaulike relative-yield behavior, and nonmonotonic time evolution of the enhancement factor. These features are not always reproduced by conventional descriptions based solely on a static electron-screening potential. In this work, a phase-sensitive, observable-level framework is developed in which the reaction response arises from the coherent superposition of a slowly varying background amplitude and a possible narrow near-threshold <math><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math> contribution. Within this framework, local environment-dependent variations of the relative interference phase are represented phenomenologically by a distribution of effective resonance conditions. The measured response is consequently described as an ensemble average over locally different interference patterns, without requiring the intrinsic nuclear pole to acquire a material-dependent displacement or width. For the reported Pd and PdD relative yields, a core phase-sensitive model combining electron screening with a distributed coherent near-threshold contribution gives <math><mrow><msup><mi>χ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>13.26</mn></mrow></math> for 13 degrees of freedom, compared with <math><mrow><msup><mi>χ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>43.10</mn></mrow></math> for 20 degrees of freedom for the strict screening-only description. Among the tested static parametrizations, the core model provides the best overall balance between fit quality and model complexity. More flexible extensions containing explicit effective-condition and barrier modifications reduce the raw <math><msup><mi>χ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> only modestly, are strongly penalized by the information criteria, and drive several nuisance parameters to their imposed bounds. A joint profile of the core model gives the conditional central effective resonance condition <math><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><msubsup><mn>11</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.62</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.39</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> keV above the <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow></math> threshold in the center-of-mass system. This result is conditional on the adopted <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mspace width="0.16em"/><mi>eV</mi></mrow></math> amplitude-level width scale and the imposed bound <math><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>res</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow></math>. It should not be interpreted as a model-independent determination of a bare <math><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>4</mn></mmultiscripts></math> pole energy or as evidence for an additional narrow nuclear level. The reported time-dependent enhancement is summarized by an empirical rise-and-decay parametrization, with a relatively rapid buildup followed by a slower relaxation. This nonmonotonic behavior is compatible with an evolving target environment, but the limited time-series data do not identify a unique microscopic mechanism or independently establish an environment-induced nuclear phase shift. The results show that a distributed coherent contribution provides a viable phenomenological extension of the conventional static-screening description for the observables examined. They do not establish the existence of an additional narrow <math><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math> level and do not exclude explanations based on the known multilevel structure of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>4</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, target evolution, or other nonequilibrium effects.
